# SCIO SUB-CACHE: MASTER BUSINESS TRACKER
## Sources: 1.7a/b (Master Business Tracker)
**Last Updated:** March 13, 2026 | **Status:** PRIMED (load when building tracking/dashboard content)

---

## OVERVIEW

The Master Business Tracker is a Google Sheet that consolidates all KPIs, P&L data, and constraint analysis into one operational dashboard.

**Source file:** 1.7b - Master Business Tracker - Google Sheet.xlsx (2.6MB)
**Note:** This is a large Excel file. Load the actual file only when building tracker-related deliverables.

---

## WHAT IT TRACKS

Based on the transcript (1.7a), the tracker consolidates:

### Marketing/Acquisition Metrics
- Ad spend (daily, weekly, monthly)
- CPQBC (cost per qualified booked call)
- Lead volume and quality
- Show-up rates
- Close rates
- Cash collected %
- Cash ROAS and Revenue ROAS

### P&L Metrics
- Revenue (new + recurring)
- Marketing costs (% of revenue)
- Labor costs by department (fulfillment, sales, ops, finance)
- Overhead
- NOI %

### Client Metrics
- Active client count
- New clients signed
- Churn rate
- Ascension rate (trial → core → backend)
- Client results/satisfaction

### LTGP:CAC Components
- CAC calculation
- LTV calculation
- COGs tracking
- LTGP:CAC ratio

---

## HOW IT'S USED

- Monthly reconciliation (by 3rd-4th of following month)
- Each month = separate tab
- Theory of Constraints exercise: which metric is below KPI?
- Decision-making: where to invest resources, who to hire, when to scale spend

---

## APW APPLICATION NOTES

### For APW Course
Students will need a simplified version of this tracker adapted to credit/funding business metrics:
- Applications submitted
- Funding approved (amount + count)
- Fees collected
- Client retention/ascension through tiers
- Marketing spend (if running ads)
- Fulfillment costs (if DFY)

### For Building This Deliverable
When the time comes to create APW's version of this tracker:
1. Read the actual 1.7b Excel file for structure/layout
2. Adapt columns to APW-specific metrics
3. Keep the P&L structure aligned with SCIO targets (same department %s apply)
